content.text:
## Implementing: bolt-abc (schema: loopdemo)

**Progress before this run:** 1/4 tasks complete (task 4, `retire legacy-shim in cortex-kit`, already done).

The apply instructions for this change specify a construction loop run as a Claude Code dynamic workflow — fan-out is the workflow's job, not one-at-a-time work here. Workflow launched (`wf_1b4ad933-4b8`), running in the background.

**Shape of the workflow:**

- **Analyse phase** — an agent runs `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` fresh each pass and infers, from the task descriptions alone, which not-done tasks are startable and which are blocked. Nothing in the data declares dependencies.
- **Build phase** — one agent per startable task, each writing `out/<task-id>.txt` with the line `built <task-id>`.
- **Passes** — the loop re-queries each pass rather than reusing the prior answer. Tasks built earlier in the run are fed forward into the analyse prompt, so a task blocked on a just-built one becomes startable on the next pass. It stops when a pass turns up nothing new startable (capped at 6 passes as a runaway guard).

One thing worth flagging: the build step, as specified, only writes a marker file — it doesn't check the task off in `tasks.md`. That's why the loop tracks built ids in-script; without it, re-querying would return the same unchecked tasks forever. I'll update the `tasks.md` checkboxes here once the workflow reports back.

I'll report which tasks got built and which are still waiting when it completes.

content.text:
## Implementation Complete

**Change:** bolt-abc
**Schema:** loopdemo
**Progress:** 4/4 tasks complete ✓

### How it ran

The loop executed as a dynamic workflow (`wf_1b4ad933-4b8`) — 6 agents, 3 passes, ~43s. Each pass re-ran `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` rather than reusing the prior pass's answer.

**Pass 1** — analyse found tasks 1 and 2 startable, 3 waiting:
- `1` gateway-auth — nothing else in the list is a prerequisite
- `2` rocs-record-split — self-contained in rocs-kit
- `3` devportal-caller — waits on task 1; it consumes the gateway-auth endpoint task 1 produces

Two build agents ran in parallel → `out/1.txt`, `out/2.txt`.

**Pass 2** — re-query; with gateway-auth built, task 3 became startable → `out/3.txt`.

**Pass 3** — nothing startable, nothing waiting. Loop exited.

The dependency between 3 and 1 was never declared in the data — the analyse agent inferred it from the description text, which is what the instructions called for.

### Verified

All three markers exist with the expected single line:

```
out/1.txt: built 1
out/2.txt: built 2
out/3.txt: built 3
```

### Completed This Session
- [x] build gateway-auth in atlas-kit
- [x] build rocs-record-split in rocs-kit
- [x] build devportal-caller in atlas-kit, which calls the gateway-auth endpoint and cannot start until gateway-auth is built

(Task 4, `retire legacy-shim in cortex-kit`, was already done before this session.)

Nothing is still waiting. `openspec list` now reports the change as `complete` — you can archive it with `/opsx:archive`.

One note on the design, since it matters if you re-run this: the build step as specified only writes `out/<id>.txt` and does not check tasks off in `tasks.md`. The workflow therefore tracked built ids in-script and fed them into each pass's analyse prompt — without that, re-querying would return the same unchecked tasks indefinitely and task 3 would never unblock. I updated the `tasks.md` checkboxes here after verifying the markers.

This repo isn't a git repository, so I made no commit.

## Implementing: bolt-abc (schema: loopdemo)

**Progress before this run:** 1/4 tasks complete (task 4, `retire legacy-shim in cortex-kit`, already done).

The apply instructions for this change specify a construction loop run as a Claude Code dynamic workflow — fan-out is the workflow's job, not one-at-a-time work here. Workflow launched (`wf_1b4ad933-4b8`), running in the background.

**Shape of the workflow:**

- **Analyse phase** — an agent runs `openspec instructions apply --change bolt-abc --json` fresh each pass and infers, from the task descriptions alone, which not-done tasks are startable and which are blocked. Nothing in the data declares dependencies.
- **Build phase** — one agent per startable task, each writing `out/<task-id>.txt` with the line `built <task-id>`.
- **Passes** — the loop re-queries each pass rather than reusing the prior answer. Tasks built earlier in the run are fed forward into the analyse prompt, so a task blocked on a just-built one becomes startable on the next pass. It stops when a pass turns up nothing new startable (capped at 6 passes as a runaway guard).

One thing worth flagging: the build step, as specified, only writes a marker file — it doesn't check the task off in `tasks.md`. That's why the loop tracks built ids in-script; without it, re-querying would return the same unchecked tasks forever. I'll update the `tasks.md` checkboxes here once the workflow reports back.

I'll report which tasks got built and which are still waiting when it completes.
